Consistency across production batches is non-negotiable. Demand for Indian ceramic tiles Germany has grown significantly, particularly from the Morbi manufacturing cluster. text_content: Germany’s Unglazed Ceramic Tiles Market 2025: Import Trends, Prices & Supplier Insights Visual for Germany’s Market for Unglazed Ceramic Tiles in 2024-2025 July 10, 2025 Germany’s Market for Unglazed Ceramic Tiles in 2024-2025 Market analysis for: Germany Product analysis: 6907 - Ceramic flags and paving, hearth or wall tiles; ceramic mosaic cubes and the like, whether or not on a backing; finishing ceramics Industry: Chemicals Report type: Product–Country Report Pages: 66 Main source of data: UN Comtrade Database Download Full Report (PDF) Access Market Reports $19.99 / 30 days unlimited or generate your own across 6,000+ goods x 100+ countries in real time. Germany’s Market for Unglazed Ceramic Tiles in 2024-2025: Southern Supplier Dominance, Price Erosion, and Diverging Trade Trajectories In 2024, Germany imported USD 720.7 million worth of unglazed ceramic tiles (HS Code 6907), totaling 1.27 million tons . The five-year CAGR for import value stands at -4.38% , with volumes declining at -3.17% , reflecting a long-term contraction. Proxy prices also fell by -1.25% CAGR , reaching USD 561.16/ton in the LTM period. Despite this, short-term trends indicate a rebound, with 27.3% YoY volume growth and 15.4% value growth in early 2025. Italy led as the top supplier, accounting for 50.05% of import value, followed by Spain, Poland, Türkiye, and Czechia. Domestic production remains limited, specialized in niche applications. Market entry remains competitive, with potential new supplier expansion capped at USD 1.25 million/month , conditional on price or quality advantages. Overall, the market reflects a dual dynamic: tactical short-term growth amid structural long-term decline. 1. HS Code Description & Industrial Role: Framing the Product’s Global Relevance HS Code 6907 refers to: “Ceramic flags and paving, hearth or wall tiles; ceramic mosaic cubes and the like, whether or not on a backing; finishing ceramics.” This product category encompasses unglazed ceramic tiles used extensively in residential, commercial, and industrial construction. Their functions span: Floor and wall applications (paving, hearths, bathrooms, facades) Architectural finishes in both interior and exterior settings Urban infrastructure such as walkways, public transport stations, and plaza flooring These tiles are favored for their durability, thermal resistance, and slip resistance , especially in high-traffic or high-moisture environments. Key end-use sectors include: Real estate and building construction Public infrastructure and urban development Hospitality and retail interiors Industrial facilities (factories, warehouses) Policy Developments: Germany, as an EU member, is subject to several import tariff and trade defense mechanisms . Notably: The EU imposed definitive anti-dumping duties on ceramic tiles from India and Türkiye in February 2023 (4.8%–20.9% for Türkiye; 6.7%–8.7% for India). No preferential duties were granted by Germany for imports of this HS Code in 2023. A zero percent share of these imports entered Germany duty-free in 2023. 2. Market Overview: Germany’s Imports of Unglazed Ceramics in Context Market Size and Trends (2024) Metric Value Import Value USD 720.7 million Import Volume 1,266.31 thousand tons 5-Year CAGR (Value) -4.38% 5-Year CAGR (Volume) -3.17% Proxy Price (Avg.) USD 0.57/kg Proxy Price CAGR (5Y) -1.25% Share in Total Imports 0.05% Change in Share Over 5Y -31.58% Germany’s import market for unglazed ceramics has been in a long-term contraction phase , driven by both declining demand and declining prices . Despite the five-year downturn, short-term indicators showed a modest rebound : Jan–Feb 2025 import value reached USD 130.13 million, marking a +15.38% YoY growth . The same period saw a 27.33% volume increase , rising to 227.93 Ktons. However, proxy prices continued their downward trajectory , averaging USD 561.16/ton in LTM (Mar 2024–Feb 2025), down -10.07% YoY , consistent with a stagnating price trend . Figure 1. Germany's Market Size of Unglazed ceramics in M US$ (left axis) and Annual Growth Rates in % (right axis) 3. Global Context: Key Suppliers in a Changing Trade Environment The global import market for HS Code 6907—Unglazed Ceramic Tiles—amounted to USD 10.06 billion in 2024 , with a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of +3.3% in value terms over the 2020–2024 period. In volume terms, however, the market was stagnant , with a CAGR of -2.82% , pointing to a structural shift from volume-driven to value-driven trade. Major Importing Nations in 2024 (by Value Share) Country Share of Global Imports (%) YoY Growth (2024) United States 22.61% -4.17% Germany 7.36% -8.45% Philippines 5.25% -15.3% Republic of Korea 4.56% +2.56% Australia 4.13% +19.22% Germany ranked second globally , accounting for 7.36% of global imports . Despite this, Germany’s year-on-year import value fell sharply by -8.45% , indicating weakened national demand relative to its international peers. The overall market driver in recent years has been a decline in demand counterbalanced by increasing prices , producing a relatively stable value trajectory despite falling volumes. Notably, France, UK, Saudi Arabia, Indonesia, and Poland were excluded from full global market calculation due to irregular trade data reporting, suggesting potential data blind spots in broader market analysis. Figure 2. Global Market Size (B US$, left axes), Annual Growth Rates (%, right axis) 4. Pricing Trends: Declining Proxy Prices Undermining Market Value Germany's import market for unglazed ceramics has been marked by a downward trend in proxy prices , further exacerbating the contraction in import values. LTM average price was USD 561.16/ton , with five monthly price points lower than any observed over the past four years, signaling record low price benchmarks. Short-term Forecast: Proxy prices are expected to continue declining at a monthly rate of -0.66% (equivalent to -7.68% annually), underpinned by stagnant demand conditions. While volume growth in late 2024 and early 2025 slightly rebounded, the continued erosion of price levels suggests limited margin expansion potential for exporters entering or operating in the German market under current conditions. 5. Key Suppliers & Competitive Landscape: Concentrated Market Led by Southern Europe In the LTM period (March 2024 – February 2025), Germany imported USD 738.06 million worth of unglazed ceramic tiles. Title: Floor Tiles & Wall Tiles Manufacturer in Germany

URL Source: https://adilaceramic.com/pages/floor-tiles-wall-tiles-manufacturer-in-germany

Markdown Content:
Germany is globally recognized for engineering precision, technological advancement, and uncompromising quality standards. These strengths extend seamlessly into the tile industry, making the country a preferred destination for premium floor tiles and wall tiles. From modern residential interiors to large-scale commercial and industrial projects, tile manufacturers in Germany are trusted for durability, consistency, and innovative design.

With advanced manufacturing facilities, strict EU regulations, and a strong focus on sustainability, Germany has positioned itself as a reliable tiles supplier for global markets. In this detailed guide, we explore the German tile manufacturing landscape, tile types, technological advancements, export opportunities, comparisons with other European manufacturers, and a brand spotlight on Adila Ceramic.

## Why Germany Is a Global Hub for Tile Manufacturing

Germany’s manufacturing reputation is built on precision, automation, and continuous innovation. Tile manufacturers in Germany invest heavily in modern production lines, digital printing technologies, and quality control systems that ensure uniformity across every tile produced.

Strict adherence to European Union standards ensures that ceramic tiles Germany produces meet high benchmarks for durability, safety, and environmental responsibility. These regulations cover aspects such as water absorption, slip resistance, chemical resistance, and mechanical strength critical for both **[ceramic floor tiles](https://adilaceramic.com/type/wall-tiles/1)** and porcelain wall tiles.

Additionally, Germany’s central European location provides excellent logistical advantages, enabling faster and more cost-efficient exports across Europe and beyond. This combination of quality, compliance, and accessibility makes Germany a leading global tiles hub.

## Overview of the German Tile Manufacturing Industry

The German **[tile manufacturing industry](https://adilaceramic.com/pages/floor-tiles-wall-tiles-manufacturer-in-spain)** has evolved significantly over the past few decades. Traditional ceramic craftsmanship has merged with advanced automation and digital design technologies to meet modern architectural demands.

Today, German manufacturers produce a wide variety of:

**•**Ceramic tiles

**•**Porcelain tiles

**•**Large format tiles

**•**Specialized technical and outdoor tiles

These products serve residential housing, commercial developments, public infrastructure, and industrial facilities. German tiles are widely used in airports, hospitals, shopping centers, hotels, and high-end residential projects.

The industry also has a strong export orientation, supplying high-quality floor tiles and wall tiles to Europe, the Middle East, Asia, Africa, and North America.

## Types of Floor Tiles Manufactured in Germany

![Image 1: Types of Floor Tiles Manufactured in Germany](https://adilaceramic.com/uploads/pages/Dynamic_Content_695f473689398.webp)

### Ceramic Floor Tiles

Ceramic floor tiles are a popular choice for residential applications due to their affordability, design versatility, and ease of maintenance. German ceramic tiles stand out for their consistent thickness, smooth edges, and long-lasting surface finishes.

These tiles are commonly used in living rooms, bedrooms, **[kitchens](https://adilaceramic.com/space/kitchen/1)**, and light-traffic commercial spaces.

### Porcelain Floor Tiles

Porcelain tiles are known for their high density, low porosity, and superior strength. German-manufactured porcelain floor tiles are ideal for heavy-traffic environments such as malls, offices, hotels, and transportation hubs.

Their resistance to moisture, stains, and wear makes them a preferred option for long-term installations.

### Vitrified Floor Tiles

Vitrified tiles undergo a specialized manufacturing process that enhances strength and stain resistance. These tiles offer a refined aesthetic and are often used in modern interiors that require both durability and elegance.

### Outdoor & Anti-Slip Floor Tiles

German **[tile manufacturers](https://adilaceramic.com/pages/floor-tiles-wall-tiles-manufacturer-in-united-kingdom)** also produce outdoor-grade tiles designed to withstand extreme weather conditions. Anti-slip finishes make these tiles suitable for balconies, terraces, patios, and poolside areas.

## Types of Wall Tiles Manufactured in Germany

![Image 2: Types of Wall Tiles Manufactured in Germany](https://adilaceramic.com/uploads/pages/Dynamic_Content_695f47524634f.webp)

### Ceramic Wall Tiles

Ceramic wall tiles remain a staple in kitchens, bathrooms, and utility spaces. Lightweight and easy to install, they offer excellent moisture resistance and hygienic properties.

### Porcelain Wall Tiles

Porcelain wall tiles are increasingly used in luxury interiors due to their premium finish and superior durability. They are ideal for high-humidity environments such as bathrooms and spas.

### Decorative & Designer Wall Tiles

German manufacturers offer a wide range of decorative wall tiles featuring textures, patterns, and 3D surfaces. These tiles help create visually striking feature walls in both residential and commercial spaces.

### Large Format Wall Tiles

Large format tiles are a growing trend in modern architecture. They provide a seamless, minimalistic appearance with fewer grout lines, making spaces appear larger and more refined.

## Key Features of German-Manufactured Floor & Wall Tiles

German floor tiles and wall tiles are globally valued for their superior performance and refined aesthetics. Key features include:

**•**Precision manufacturing with minimal dimensional variation

**•**High resistance to scratches, stains, and chemicals

**•**Low water absorption for enhanced durability

**•**Wide range of finishes including matte, gloss, stone-look, and wood-look

**•**Compliance with international quality and safety standards

These characteristics make German tiles ideal for long-term, high-value projects.

## Sustainability & Eco-Friendly Tile Manufacturing in Germany

Sustainability plays a crucial role in the German tile industry. Many tile manufacturers use energy-efficient kilns, water recycling systems, and eco-friendly raw materials to reduce environmental impact.

German ceramic tiles and **[porcelain tiles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porcelain_tile)** often meet stringent EU environmental regulations, ensuring reduced carbon emissions and responsible waste management. This focus on sustainability not only benefits the environment but also adds long-term value for developers and end users.

## Technology & Innovation in German Tile Manufacturing

Advanced technology is at the heart of German tile production. Digital inkjet printing allows manufacturers to replicate natural materials such as marble, granite, and wood with exceptional realism.

Automation ensures consistent quality, while advanced surface treatments improve slip resistance, durability, and ease of maintenance. Continuous research and development help German manufacturers stay ahead of global design and performance trends.

## Applications of Floor & Wall Tiles

![Image 3: Applications of Floor & Wall Tiles](https://adilaceramic.com/uploads/pages/Dynamic_Content_695f47703b9c1.webp)

German-manufactured tiles are used across a wide range of applications, including:

**•**Residential homes and apartments

**•**Commercial offices, hotels, and retail outlets

**•**Public buildings such as hospitals and schools

**•**Industrial facilities and outdoor environments

Their versatility makes them suitable for both indoor and outdoor use.

Ceramic tiles are made of clay, silica, dyes, and many other materials. They are thin, though some can be up to 20 mm thick. Raw materials are ground and compressed through different methods and undergo several heating and cooling processes. The combination of various materials and manufacturing processes leads to the production of tiles with mixed characteristics. Fired clay is the most common and is obtained using the semi-dry pressing technique with one or more firings. The surface is coated, offering various colors and designs. Rapid urbanization and infrastructure development are increasing the demand for ceramic tiles in different construction projects. The durability of ceramic tiles makes them an ideal choice for the residential and commercial sectors. KEY TAKEAWAYS BY TYPE The ceramic tiles market by type includes porcelain and ceramic. Porcelain dominates the market in terms of demand, as its density makes it more resistant to wear and tear. BY APPLICATION The ceramic tiles market by application includes flooring, interior walls, exterior walls, and other applications. Flooring is the fastest-growing segment because of its superior strength, water resistance, and low maintenance requirements. BY END-USE SECTOR The ceramic tiles market by end-use sector includes residential and non- residential. Residential dominates the market in terms of demand, due to the increasing working population and millennials aspiring to homeownership. BY REGION The market in the Middle East & Africa is expected to grow the fastest, driven by population growth, urbanization, and increased demand for good infrastructure. COMPETITIVE LANDSCAPE The market is driven by strategic product launches, collaborations, acquisitions, and expansions from leading players such as Mohawk Industries, Inc., Grupo Lamosa, Siam Cement Public Company Limited, Pamesa Ceramica, RAK Ceramics, and Ceramica Carmelo Fior. These companies are strong in their home regions and are exploring geographic diversification options to grow their businesses. Technological advancements in tile manufacturing and rising demand for ceramic tiles in emerging markets are expected to create growth opportunities for companies in the ceramic tiles market. However, the natural gas crisis and intense competition are expected to be the challenges for the market players. TRENDS & DISRUPTIONS IMPACTING CUSTOMERS' CUSTOMERS Changes in customer trends and disruptions impact consumers' businesses. These trends and disruptions directly affect the end consumers of tile buyers, such as homeowners, real estate developers, and businesses. At the same time, disruptions like fluctuating raw material costs, digital design tools, and innovations in installation methods are pushing tile manufacturers and distributors to adapt quickly. Source: Secondary Research, Interviews with Experts, MarketsandMarkets Analysis MARKET DYNAMICS Drivers Impact Level Increasing population & urbanization Growing investments in the construction industry RESTRAINTS Impact Level Volatile raw raw material prices Increasing regulations, tariffs, and anti-dumping measures OPPORTUNITIES Impact Level Office-to-residential conversions unlock new growth avenues for the ceramic tiles market Introduction of 3D tiles and digital technologies printing CHALLENGES Impact Level Natural gas crisis in different regions Extremely competitive market Source: Secondary Research, Interviews with Experts, MarketsandMarkets Analysis Driver: Increasing investments in infrastructure development The increasing investments in the infrastructure sector are expected to drive the growth of the ceramic tiles market. Governments of different countries are investing in developing and upgrading infrastructure, including residential, commercial, and public properties. These developments have increased the demand for ceramic tiles—a vital construction material. As per the International Monetary Fund (IMF), it is estimated that the spending required to meet the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in 2030 will amount to USD 2.6 trillion, or 2.5% of the 2030 world GDP, in 121 emerging economies and low-income developing countries. Ceramic tiles are known for their versatility and durability. They are more sustainable than vinyl tiles and are available in various designs. These tiles are ideal for flooring and wall applications in different construction projects. The surge in infrastructure development has increased the need for high-quality tiles, boosting the growth of the ceramic tiles market. Restraint: Volatile raw material prices Different raw materials, such as clay and feldspar, are used to make ceramic tiles. Raw material prices fluctuate because of supply chain constraints in different regions, geopolitical tensions, war situations (the recent US sanctions on Russian goods), and the implementation of strict environmental regulations. Such scenarios lead to higher production costs. It is difficult for manufacturers to keep prices stable. Additionally, the increasing prices can squeeze profit margins, making it harder for firms to invest in new technologies and research. Opportunity: High demand in Asia Pacific According to the World Bank, new climate-smart infrastructure could cost low-income and middle-income countries almost 2–8% (USD 640 billion–USD 2.7 trillion) of GDP annually by 2030. The emerging markets are expected to account for most of the projected increase in infrastructure spending by 2050. Asia Pacific has witnessed expansion in its manufacturing capabilities and has a large, skilled workforce. Besides, the region has an abundant base of raw materials. Hence, it offers opportunities for ceramic tile manufacturers and suppliers looking to capitalize on the region's increasing demand. Challenge: Natural gas crisis in different regions The Russia-Ukraine war has affected many industries and sectors globally, including the ceramic tiles industry. The fluctuations and increased natural gas prices are the major challenges in the current scenario. Natural gas constitutes 30–40% of the production cost of ceramic tiles. Hence, it is a critical energy source for firing kilns. The increase in its price directly raises production costs. The ceramic tiles industry requires a significant gas daily and is therefore becoming highly vulnerable to price volatility. The increased costs are expected to consequently raise the prices of ceramic tiles, reducing demand and squeezing the profit margins of manufacturers. text_content: Sectors | Cerame-Unie - The European Ceramic Industry Association Home Contact Us Sectors Cerame-Unie is an umbrella organisation representing the European ceramic industry structured in nine ceramic sectors. Cerame-Unie holds the secretariat of both the umbrella association and seven of its sectors. The secretariats of the remaining three sectors are in Hagen (EEA), Paris (FEPA), and Brussels (EXCA) . Our members and associate members, both federations of national associations and direct members, are established in 30 European countries, including 27 EU Member States. The ceramic industry is reported as gathering about 2000 companies in the EU, including not only large international groups but also a large proportion of SMEs (80%) from nine different sectors, truly embodying the European motto, “ United in diversity ”. According to article 5 of the Cerame-Unie by-laws, "the association is open to European Federations bringing together National Federations or National Federations interested in ceramic industry, or, for lack of those, private companies active in the ceramic industry or whose business is linked to the ceramic industry". Brick and roof tiles Wall and floor tiles Table- and Ornamentalware Sanitaryware Refractories Technical Ceramics Clay pipes Expanded clay Abrasives Flower Pots Brick and roof tiles TBE - Tiles and Bricks Europe Tiles & Bricks Europe (TBE) was founded in 1952 in Zürich and registered as an international non-profit organisation (AISBL) under Belgian law in 2008. TBE represents industry associations and companies from 21 EU Member States and Switzerland. The association promotes interests of clay bricks and roof tiles industry in Europe. It provides a forum for its members to exchange information on technical development, sustainable construction, climate change, resource efficiency and other emerging issues. It represents over 700 companies, which employ around 50,000 people and generate a production value of around €5.5 billion. In Europe there are around 1,300 production sites located near quarries which provide local jobs and keep transport emissions low. Please consult the TBE website for more detailed information on the association and its products. TBE WEbsite Murray Rattana-Ngam President Mirosław Jaroszewicz Vice-President Magdalena Vallebona Secretary General Wall and floor tiles CET - European Ceramic Tile Manufacturers Federation Wall and floor ceramic tiles constitute the biggest sector in terms of turnover among European ceramic industries with total sales in 2009 estimated around € 9 billion. Although Italy and Spain are by far the two biggest producers in the EU, significant production also exists in Poland, Portugal, Germany, France, Bulgaria, the UK, Romania, the Netherlands, Czech Republic and Hungary. One third of the production in ceramic tiles is exported outside of the EU, resulting in a largely positive trade balance with exports representing in value around four times the EU imports in ceramic tiles. At international level, CET holds the secretariat of the World Ceramic Tiles Forum. Graziano Verdi President Roman Blažíček Vice-President Raúl Carnicer Vice-President Renaud Batier Secretary General Table- and Ornamentalware FEPF - European Federation of Ceramic Table- and Ornamentalware The European Federation of Ceramic Table- and Ornamentalware (FEPF) is a member association of Cerame-Unie. It was founded in 1959 and its secretariat is based in Brussels. Its membership currently covers producers in France, Germany, Italy, United Kingdom, Spain, Portugal, Poland, Romania, Croatia and Hungary. FEPF developed contacts with the industry in other countries e.g. in Czech Republic as well as in countries where no national associations exist (e.g. Austria, Bulgaria, Lithuania and Slovenia.) The sector employs 25,000 skilled people. Charles Bernardaud President Raúl Graña Vice-President Omid Majidi Ahi Secretary General Sanitaryware FECS - European Sanitaryware Producers Federation Established in Geneva in 1954, the European Sanitaryware Producers Federation (FECS) promotes the interests of the ceramic sanitaryware industry in Europe. Today it represents seven national trade associations and ten companies from 15 countries (European Union, Turkey and Switzerland). FECS directly employs approximately 22,000 people and has an annual turnover of € 4.5 billion. To learn more and to find detailed information, please consult the FECS website. FECS Website Pau Abelló Pellicer President Anne-Claire Bruant Secretary General Refractories PRE - Producers of Refractories in Europe The European Refractories Producers Federation (PRE) is the representative organization of the European refractory industry, founded in 1953. PRE unites members from 16 countries, from Sweden to Italy, from the UK to Poland. Four multi-national companies, namely Calderys, Magnesita, Refratechnik and Vesuvius, are also direct members. PRE represents an annual turnover of € 3.5 billion and employs nearly 20,000 people. PRE has a sector specific website where you can find further information on its members, standardization, REACH and raw materials. PRE Website Matthias Stalzer President Daniela Vigilante Secretary General Technical Ceramics EuTeCer - European Technical Ceramics Federation The European Technical Ceramics Federation (EuTeCer) represents the technical ceramics industry in Europe, with members in the UK, France, Italy, Germany, Romania and Turkey. Carsten Russner President Daniela Vigilante Secretary General Clay pipes FEUGRES - European Federation of Clay Pipe Producers The European Vitrified Clay Pipe Federation (FEUGRES) represents the vitrified clay pipe industry in Europe and was founded in 1957 in Switzerland. FEUGRES has members from Belgium, Germany, the United Kingdom, Italy, the Netherlands, Austria and Switzerland. Further information can be found on the FEUGRES website . FEUGRES Website Johan van der Biest President Expanded clay EXCA - European Expanded Clay Association European Expanded Clay Association (EXCA) was established in 2007 as an asbl, a non-profit making organisation, under Belgian law. EXCA represents and promotes the interests of the European producers of expanded clay. Today, 10 companies operating 11 plants in 10 European countries (Norway, Denmark, UK, Poland, Portugal, Italy, Belgium, Germany, Czech Republic, Finland) are members. Through its members, EXCA represents more than 90% of the production in Europe. Visit the EXCA website to find out more. EXCA Website Kim Rosenbom President Mara Caboara Secretary General Abrasives FEPA - Federation of European Producers of Abrasives The Federation of European Producers of Abrasives (FEPA) represents the European abrasive industry since its inception in 1955, encompassing four product segments, bonded & coated abrasives, superabrasives and grains. FEPA members cover 90% of the European production of abrasive products. Visit the FEPA website to find out more. FEPA Website Flower Pots

Company The power of ceramics From mosaic tiles to ceramic facades – Deutsche Steinzeug Solar Ceramics GmbH is the specialist for residential, swimming pool, and facade ceramics. With our Agrob Buchtal product brand, we are not only the market leader in Germany, but also one of the world's leading manufacturers in the field of ceramic covering materials. We focus on innovation, design, sustainability, and product quality "Made in Germany." We offer our customers a high-quality and comprehensive range of products, expert advice, and custom-made products. Mission Market leader as a "ceramic problem solver" Wall and floor tiles, swimming pool ceramics, and ceramic facades—our core competencies lie in the high quality and diversity of our product range, our consulting expertise, and our service orientation. The Deutsche Steinzeug Group has been the market leader in the ceramic covering materials business segment since 1999 and is also one of the leading manufacturers internationally. We serve more than 120,000 architects and planners worldwide, offering them a range of colors and formats specially designed for commercial construction with our Agrob Buchtal brand, as well as comprehensive advice with our architect service. We deliver our architectural ceramics to almost 100 countries. We see ourselves as "ceramic problem solvers" for our customers and also produce custom-made products on request. The easy-to-clean, antibacterial Hytect surface, which we introduced back in 2000, is a prime example of our company's innovative spirit. Our customer and service orientation extends beyond our product range and consulting services to include the shipping of our goods: for example, thanks to the special customs authorization (AEO-F) of the EU Customs Code, our freight shipments are processed more quickly. Locations Deeply rooted in tradition, globally networked Deutsche Steinzeug Solar Ceramics GmbH is a historically grown group. Our roots date back to 1755, and we were first listed on the stock exchange in 1896. Production takes place primarily at our German locations in Ötzingen, Schwarzenfeld, Sinzig, Witterschlick, and Bremerhaven. With around 1,000 highly qualified and experienced employees worldwide and modern manufacturing processes, we ensure that our comprehensive product range and services relating to ceramic covering materials are consistently maintained at the highest level and continuously developed. The Deutsche Steinzeug Group has its own sales organizations in Germany, France, Switzerland, and the USA, as well as a global network of local partners. Both companies initially focused exclusively on the production of stoneware sewer construction products. The production program was subsequently expanded to include the manufacture of acid-resistant articles and apparatus made of stoneware for the chemical industry. The companies quickly developed into the leading producers of heavy clay products. By 1926, Cremer & Breuer had acquired a majority stake in Deutsche Steinzeugwarenfabrik Aktiengesellschaft and, at the beginning of the 1930s, prompted the latter to acquire a majority stake in "Annawerk Schamotte- und Tonwarenfabrik AG" in Oeslau. Soon afterwards, Annawerk AG founded Buchtal AG in Schwarzenfeld/Upper Palatinate. These shareholding transactions created a group whose main field of activity was in heavy clay ceramics and included the manufacture of vitrified clay pipes, tiles and slabs as well as other products such as refractory materials, roof tiles, etc. The great demand for stoneware pipes during the reconstruction phase in post-war Germany opened up good market opportunities for this product area. This was therefore the first investment focus. At the same time, Buchtal AG specialized in ceramic tiles and slabs and over the years became a specialist supplier of contract ceramics. In order to increase competitiveness and become a full-range ceramic supplier, Deutsche Steinzeug acquired the tile-producing companies of the AGROB Group in 1992 and 50.4% of the Czech company RAKO a.s., Rakovnik, in 1993, which it increased to around 95% at the beginning of 1998. In 1997, the parent company Deutsche Steinzeug Solar Ceramics GmbH took over operational management again by merging the ceramic flooring materials with the holding company. In the following year, Deutsche Steinzeug AG acquired all the shares in OSTARA LAUFEN Keramik GmbH, Meerbusch, thereby strengthening the Group's contract expertise in ceramic flooring materials. In May of the same year, the stoneware pipe activities were merged with those of the Wienerberger Group through the acquisition of Keramo Wienerberger N.V., Hasselt/Belgium, making STEINZEUG Abwassersysteme GmbH the largest European stoneware pipe producer. Following approval by the European Commission in Brussels in 1999, the Wienerberger Group increased its stake from 24.9% to 50%. Since January 1, 2000, Deutsche Steinzeug AG has also only held a 50% stake in its vitrified clay pipe division. In December 1998, the company sold AnnaWerk Keramische Betriebe GmbH, Rödental (high-performance ceramics) as part of its continued focus on the two core business areas. The year 1999 was dominated by the goal of becoming the largest German ceramics producer. In order to achieve this goal, Deutsche Steinzeug AG acquired all shares in Jasba GmbH, Ötzingen, and Meissen Keramik GmbH, Meissen. This gave it market leadership in the German mosaic market (Jasba) and, for the first time, ownership of a traditional brand with a high level of consumer recognition (Meissen Keramik). Porcelaingres produces innovative porcelain stoneware wall and floor coverings at its facility south of Berlin, one of the most modern in Europe. The production process and plant technology set the standard in terms of sustainability as well as environmental and climate impact. In Vetschau, 40% of the raw materials used are sourced from recycling processes. Rainwater and production waste are collected and reused or reprocessed. Some of the company’s energy needs are covered by renewables. The 870-meter long photovoltaic system installed on the roofs of the production plants produces 2.4 MWp of electricity required for production. In recent years, state-of-the-art manufacturing, measurement and regulation technologies have reduced the production process to a few streamlined steps, with a significant reduction in CO2 emissions. Thanks to heat energy recovery from the kilns, it has been possible to reduce CO2 emissions by approximately 4,000 tons per year learn more Format variants Premium architectural ceramic surfaces that are ideal for use throughout any project thanks to the wide range of base formats, extra large sizes and special formats. While our tiles are designed to meet or exceed the Dynamic Coefficient of Friction (DCOF) requirements outlined in ANSI A326.3, maintaining the safety and functionality of the tile surface is ultimately the end-user’s responsibility. USER RESPONSIBILITY FOR MAINTENANCE AND COMPLIANCE Although our tiles have a textured finish that offers slip resistance, they are not slip-proof. It is crucial for end-users to regularly clean, maintain, and monitor their tile installations to ensure continued safety. Following the guidelines set forth by ASTM F1637 and ANSI A1264.2 standards is essential to prevent slip-and-fall incidents. These standards provide the necessary framework for maintaining safe walking surfaces and ensuring slip resistance in working environments. RECOMMENDED MAINTENANCE PRACTICES Regular Cleaning: Refer to the Argelith Cleaning Guidelines for detailed instructions on daily cleaning routines, including the use of neutral cleaners and proper equipment. Monitoring: Regular inspections should be conducted to assess slip resistance, with annual DCOF testing recommended to comply with ANSI A326.3. Use of Protective Measures: Placing walk-off mats at entrances and transitions between wet and dry areas can minimize the spread of contaminants and provide protection against slipping. By adhering to these standards and maintaining your tile installation, you not only extend the life of your flooring but also ensure it remains a safe and functional surface for everyone. # Table of content 3 www.BL2020.com 

# Sources and Definitions 

Data collection and generation :

▪ Trade  statistics  from  UN  Comtrade  *

▪ Production  statistics  from  Destatis /Genesis 

▪ Expert  Interviews  (verification  of  production  and  trade  figures  and  sales  development) 

▪ Ceramic  tile  producers 

▪ Trade  (ceramic  tiles)                                                                         

> *UN Comtrade receives trade data from EUROSTAT, which in turn receives its data from the statistical offices of
> the individual member states (for DE it is Destatis ).Since the sources of data of all individual EU countries are
> the national authorities of each of the member states, and since the source of EU data is Eurostat, there can be
> differences between reconstructed EU from individual country data in UN Comtrade and the combined EU from
> EUROSTAT .

For  the  import  and  export  statistics,  the  following  HS  codes  were  taken  into  account  for 

the  B+L  market  calculation :

Included  HS  Codes  (Import  and  Export) 

▪ HTS  Code : 6907 .21  - Ceramic  Flags  And  Paving,  Hearth  Or  Wall  Tiles  Of  A Water 

Absorption  Coefficient  By  Weight  Not  Exceeding  0,5 Percent 

▪ HTS  Code : 6907 .22  - Ceramic  Flags  And  Paving,  Hearth  Or  Wall  Tiles,  Of  A Water 

Absorption  Coefficient  By  Weight  Exceeding  0,5 But  Not  Exceeding  10 %

▪ HTS  Code : 6907 .22  - Ceramic  Flags  And  Paving,  Hearth  Or  Wall  Tiles,  Of  A Water 

Absorption  Coefficient  By  Weight  Exceeding  10  %

Not  included  HS  Codes  (Import  and  Export) 

▪ HTS  Code : 6907 .10  - Ceramic  Tiles,  cubes  and  similar  articles,  whether  or  not  rectangular, 

the  largest  surface  area  of  which  is  capable  of  being  enclosed  in  a square  the  side  of  which 

is  less  than  7 cm 

▪ HTS  Code : 6908 .10  - Glazed  Ceramic  Tiles,  Cubes  And  Similar  Articles,  Largest  Surface  Area 

Of  Which  Can  Be  Enclosed  In  A Square  With  Sides  Less  Than  7 Cm 

In  addition  to  the  main  data  sources  mentioned,  further  sources  of  information  are  used 

by  B+L  to  validate  the  statistics  and  forecasts .

▪ B+L  target  group  surveys : planners,  installers  (utilisation  quotes  flooring  materials  in  new 

construction/renovation,  residential  building/non  residential  building,  wall/floor  etc .)

▪ B+L  end -consumer  surveys  (mainly  on  renovation  and  substitution  trends) 

▪ Expert  surveys  (primarily  industrial) 

▪ Official  statistics  and  publications  of  various  media  (information  from  associations, 

company  reports,  editorial  departments,  newspapers,  etc .)

▪ Calculated  test  values  for  determined  quantity  structure  from  random  samples  at  the 

trade  level  (in  comparison  to  the  distribution  model) 

▪ Calculations  by  applications  on  the  basis  of  construction  and  secondary  statistics,  i.e. B+L 

Global  Building  Monitor  and  B+L  product  database  (interior  walls,  floors) 

▪ Sales  volumes  by  manufacturers 

▪ Plausibility  check  (flow  of  goods  – production/import/export  – overall  context) 

Our  data  quality  is  guaranteed  by :

▪ Specialized  industry  analysts  with  more  than  15  years’  experience  lead  our  projects 

▪ Interviews  conducted  by  qualified  and  experienced  native  speakers  with  long -standing 

connection  to  B+L 

▪ Central  research  centre  in  Bonn : all  research  (desk  research  and  telephone  interviews)  are 

conducted  at  the  Bonn  headquarters  (no  outsourcing,  no  subcontractors) 

▪ All  results  are  meticulously  double  checked 

The  prognoses  are  based  on  assumptions  regarding  the  underlying  market  conditions  (for 

example,  political  conditions) . Even  if  these  are  assessed  with  the  utmost  care  and  expertise, 

not  all  variations  can  be  predicted .4 www.BL2020.com 

# Methodology 

The  data  made  available  for  the  countries  will  be  comprehensively  comparable  due  to  the 

targeted  surveys  and  consistent  methodology . Implausibility’s  in  the  official  production  and 

trade  statistics  are  critically  examined ; subjective  dissemination  of  knowledge  from  a

publication  by  a market  participant  is  likewise  inspected . In  this  regard,  we  pursue  our  claim  to 

make  actual  market  conditions  transparent .

The  volume  trends  include  the  annual  sales  volume . The  sales  volume  is  calculated  as  the 

domestic  production  plus  import  minus  export . The  quantity  structure  for  the  reference  year 

and  the  forecasts  is  based  on  various  collection  levels  which  are  dependent  on  one  another .

The  forecasts  arise  from  the  assessment  of  the  construction  and  renovation  segments 

(determined  through  regularly  conducted  end -consumer  and  target  group  surveys),  as  well  as 

the  development  of  relevant  conditions,  e.g. political  or  economic) . At  the  same  time,  diverse 

subsidy  programs  are  considered . The  results  of  the  research  are  then  discussed  with 

manufacturers,  tradesmen,  and  branch  experts  in  the  particular  market  and  adjusted 

accordingly .

B+L  Method  of  determining  market  volume 

B+L  Distribution  model 

The  shares  of  the  distribution  channels  are  analysed  according  to  their  volumes . This,  in 

addition  to  the  assessment  of  the  traders,  requires  an  analysis  of  the  trade  structure . The 

following  distribution  channels  are  investigated :

▪ DIY 

▪ Wholesale 

▪ Specialist  trade 

▪ Direct  sales 

B+L  evaluation  model  distribution  channels :www.BL2020.com 5

# Sales of ceramic tiles in Germany 

# 2019 -2026 6 www.BL2020.com 

# Development of ceramic tiles in Germany until 2026 

[in million m²] / [ change to previous year %] 

> Source: B+L; f = Forecast; Status 10/2023

• Sales  of  ceramic  tiles  in  Germany  developed  very  positively  until 

2021 , reaching  135 ,68  million  m² .

• Since  the  end  of  2022  at  the  latest,  however,  sales  have  slumped 

significantly,  so  that  a decline  of  3,7% was  recorded  for  the  year 

as  a whole,  which  still  began  positively .

• The  current  year  2023  is  expected  to  close  with  a decline  of 

26 ,2%. For  the  time  being,  no  increase  in  sales  is  expected  next 

year  either . Increasing  sales  can  be  expected  again  at  the  end  of 

2024  and  2025  at  the  earliest .

• The  reasons  for  the  declines  since  the  end  of  2022  are  manifold :

o Increased  energy  costs  for  German  and  European 

manufacturers  due  to  the  war  in  Ukraine,  leading  to  rising 

production  costs 

o High  inflation  and  high  interest  rates  on  loans , which  is  causing 

a reluctance  to  invest  in  renovation  projects  in  the  non -energy 

sector 

o Sharp  drop  in  new  construction  (completions  and  permits), 

especially  in  the  single -family  house  sector

text_content: Tiles Exporter to Germany from India | Best Porcelain Tiles Tiles Export to Germany from India Scalane International is a trusted tiles exporter to Germany, delivering precision-engineered ceramic, porcelain, and vitrified tiles that meet strict EU and German standards. We supply high-performance tiles for Germany’s residential and commercial markets, ensuring full compliance, consistent quality, and reliable logistics. What Does Tiles Export to Germany Mean? Exporting tiles from India to Germany involves more than simply shipping a product across borders. It means supplying ceramic, porcelain, vitrified, and GVT/PGVT tiles that fully comply with EU regulatory requirements — including CE marking, EN 14411, and the EU Construction Products Regulation (CPR). German buyers expect rectified, precision-cut tiles with tight dimensional tolerances. There is strong demand for frost-resistant, anti-slip, and large-format formats, driven by both residential renovation projects and large-scale commercial developments. The supply chain typically runs from manufacturer to importer, then onward to distributor or project site — and quality must hold at every stage. Germany Tile Market Overview Germany is one of Europe’s most demanding tile markets. Compliance is non-negotiable, and consistency is expected as standard. Market Highlights Renovation work drives the majority of demand, accounting for 70–75% of total tile consumption. Porcelain tiles and large formats dominate specifications, while outdoor anti-slip tiles — rated R10 to R12 — are seeing strong growth. Tiles compatible with underfloor heating systems are also increasingly specified across both residential and commercial projects. Popular Applications German contractors and developers use tiles extensively across a wide range of settings: Residential: Bathrooms, kitchens, and living spaces Commercial: Offices, retail environments, hospitality venues, and public infrastructure Design Trends Current preferences lean toward concrete and stone looks, wood plank tiles, and matte finishes. Neutral tones — particularly grey, beige, and anthracite — remain the dominant palette across both residential and commercial segments. Types of Tiles Exported to Germany Ceramic Tiles Ceramic tiles are widely used for wall applications and light-use flooring. They offer a cost-effective solution for residential projects and remain a consistent part of the export mix. Explore: Ceramic Tiles Collection Porcelain Tiles Porcelain tiles are the most demanded category in the German market. Their low water absorption and frost-resistant properties make them suitable for both indoor and outdoor use — a key advantage in Germany’s climate. Explore: Porcelain Tiles Export Vitrified Tiles Known for their high strength and long-term durability, vitrified tiles are well-suited to commercial applications where performance under heavy foot traffic is essential. GVT / PGVT Tiles Glazed and polished glazed vitrified tiles combine technical performance with sophisticated aesthetics. With digitally printed surfaces that replicate marble, wood, and natural stone, they are increasingly specified in modern interior projects across Germany. Explore: GVT / PGVT Tiles Why Germany Imports Tiles from India India has established a strong position as a tile supplier to European markets — and Germany is no exception. The key advantages are well understood by experienced importers: A compelling cost-to-quality ratio that is difficult to match Large-scale manufacturing capacity capable of handling significant project volumes Proven expertise in large-format tiles, including sizes of 1200×2400 mm and beyond Growing alignment with EU compliance requirements Reliable bulk supply with export-ready logistics Tiles exporter to Germany – Compliance & Standards Meeting German and EU compliance requirements is not optional — it is the baseline for market entry. CE Marking CE marking is mandatory for all tiles sold in Germany. It is based on EN 14411 and requires a Declaration of Performance (DoP) to be issued by the manufacturer. EN & ISO Standards Tiles exported to Germany must meet the requirements of EN 14411 for tile classification, along with ISO 10545 test protocols covering water absorption, abrasion resistance, breaking strength, and frost resistance. DIN Standards (Germany) Germany applies additional national standards on top of EU requirements. DIN 51130 governs slip resistance, with ratings from R9 to R13. DIN 51097 applies to wet barefoot areas, using an A, B, C classification system. Additional Compliance Exporters supplying the German market should also be prepared to address the EU Construction Products Regulation (CPR), Environmental Product Declarations (EPDs), REACH compliance for chemical substances, and registration under the German Packaging Act (VerpackG / LUCID). Learn More: EU Tile Compliance Guide Quality & Precision Standards German buyers apply engineering-level expectations to tile procurement. Quality is evaluated not just on appearance, but on measurable technical performance. Key Requirements Dimensional tolerance must be within 0.5 mm. Rectified edges are considered standard, not a premium. Surface flatness must be consistent across the batch, and first-choice grading is mandatory — no grade mixing is acceptable. Technical Performance Buyers will assess breaking strength, modulus of rupture, slip resistance ratings, and water absorption figures. Each of these must be supported by third-party test documentation. Batch Consistency Shade consistency is declared using V-ratings, and calibration must be uniform across the entire consignment. German buyers expect the bulk delivery to match the approved sample — without exception. Logistics & Shipping to Germany Shipping Routes Most shipments from India to Germany depart from Mundra or Nhava Sheva and arrive at Hamburg or Bremerhaven. Rotterdam is also used as an alternative entry point, with onward distribution into Germany by road or rail. Transit Time Standard transit times run between 25 and 40 days depending on routing and port conditions. Delivery Options Scalane International can ship on FOB, CIF, or DDP terms. DDP is the preferred option for most German buyers, as it simplifies customs clearance and reduces the administrative burden on the importer. Inland Distribution Germany’s well-developed rail and road network supports fast, efficient distribution to project sites across the country and into neighbouring EU markets. Packaging & Quality Assurance Packaging Standards All shipments are packed on Euro pallets (800×1200 mm) using strong corrugated boxes with shrink wrapping and strapping applied throughout. Damage Prevention Corner protection is applied to all pallets, and moisture-resistant packaging is used as standard. Handling protocols are designed to eliminate transit damage. Quality Assurance Pre-shipment inspections are carried out on every consignment. Batch-wise test reports are provided, and calibration and shade checks are completed before loading. Learn More: Tile Export Packaging Guide Buyer Decision Factors What German Buyers Evaluate German importers and procurement teams are thorough in their supplier assessments. They will review the Technical Data Sheet (TDS) in detail, verify CE marking and DoP documentation, and check for EPD availability on sustainable projects. Consistent quality and reliable delivery timelines are weighted heavily in any supplier evaluation. Key Concerns The concerns that most often cause German buyers to switch suppliers — or walk away entirely — are quality inconsistency, compliance gaps, shipping damage, and uncertainty about long-term supplier reliability. Addressing these proactively, with documentation and audit trails, is what separates credible exporters from the rest. Press release (EN) Ceramika Paradyż has launched a company in Germany 08 kwietnia 2021 Ceramika Paradyż, one of the largest and most respected Polish enterprises producing ceramic tiles, has opened a new company in Germany – Ceramika Paradyz Deutschland GmbH. Its aim is to sell dedicated products and provide comprehensive service in Germany, Austria, Switzerland, and France. The example of Ceramika Paradyż shows that Polish production companies are doing better and better abroad. The company currently makes its offer available in over 50 countries around the world – mainly through a dealer network, and its products are associated with high quality and unique design. However, as the company's representatives point out, to operate on a larger scale, bold and comprehensive solutions are necessary. By establishing a new company, Ceramika Paradyż opens a completely new chapter and – in line with the adopted strategy – strengthens its activities in DACH markets and in France. During the first stage, it will focus on Germany - the country with the highest sales potential. This is confirmed by the data of the German Statistical Office from February this year, provided by the Polish-German Chamber of Industry and Commerce (AHK), according to which the trade turnover between Poland and Germany in 2020 amounted to EUR 122.9 billion, and Poland became the fifth most important trade partner of Germany. Ceramika Paradyz Deutschland GmbH The headquarters of the newly established company is located in Offenbach, a city with a population of over 120,000 people, located near the border of Frankfurt am Main - which is an important industrial, service and commercial centre. In the next few years, the company anticipates dynamic development, a further rise in the number of employees, and intensive marketing activities that will support sales and increase brand recognition throughout the region. Showroom Ceramikia Paradyz Deutschland GmbH So far, the only form of our presence on foreign markets has been export, which accounted for approx. 35-37% of all sales. However, we want to increase the effectiveness of our business, in accordance with the adopted development strategy. A thorough analysis confirmed our belief that the establishment of a new company is another important stage in the expansion of Ceramika Paradyż, which will allow us to strengthen the brand's position in the world and build relationships in the new business environment said Wioleta Bojdo, president of Ceramika Paradyz Deutschland GmbH. Focus on success This year, the German company will focus on developing and building a network of business partners, as well as on collaboration with architects. There are also plans to systematically develop the service in the entire German-speaking region, which will enable further expansion of the product range intended for Western markets. A prestigious company showroom has been operating in Offenbach since the end of February. It is a great place to work with B2B clients and architects who can find there a dedicated display of products from the brand's portfolio. Our showroom covers an area of approximately 300 m2 and is decorated in a tasteful loft style. Equipped with a professional display, it provides us and our clients with a high comfort of work. It is an excellent showpiece of the Paradyż brand on the German market. The equipment and design evidence the high quality of our products and the services provided by the managers we employ who have many years of experience in the industry. The first meetings with clients have already taken place there. All of them were in compliance with the sanitary regulations, of course said Tomasz Sokołowski, DACH Markets Coordinator at Ceramika Paradyż. From left: Tomasz Sokołowski, Michael Haupenthal and Giuseppe Lombardo An important element of these activities is the dedicated product portfolio, which can be seen at the display in the German Ceramika Paradyż showroom. Collections such as NATURAL ROCKS, PURE ART, RIVERSAND, OAK TIME, have been introduced especially for the needs of the local commercial area and created in consultation with the most important clients. Natural Rocks tiles collection I look forward to meeting our clients and potential partners to show them what we can do! Get ready for Paradyż! said Michael Haupenthal, Business Development Manager Pure Art tiles collection Ceramika Paradyż is a family company that has been boosting design, creating and delivering innovative products with a unique look and the highest quality for 32 years. The company is present on markets all over the world - from European countries, through Africa, the Middle East and Asia, the USA, to New Zealand. It has won the most prestigious awards in the field of design and economy - including the Red Dot Design Award 2016, iF Design 2017, Dobry Wzór 2018, 2020 and Bronze A'Design Award 2020, as well as the Economic Award of the President of the Republic of Poland, and the Annual Award of the Minister of Culture and National Heritage. Ceramika Paradyż's product collections are complementary - among them the clients can find wall and floor tiles, ceramic slabs, clinker, glass decorations and decorative elements in many sizes. The company is in the process of launching a breakthrough investment worth over PLN 125 million. In one of the production plants, a worldwide innovative demonstration line for the production of large-sized ceramic plates using the "throughout" mass dyeing technology is currently being created; the plates can be produced even in the size 1800 x 3200 mm and a thickness of up to 30 mm. The problem this actually solves Searching for "Ceramic Tiles importer Germany" does not return German importers. I ran that query early on and got, roughly in this order: Indian and Chinese tile manufacturers doing SEO against the phrase "importer Germany" B2B directories (Alibaba, IndiaMART, ExportHub) selling lead lists Trade-data vendors (Volza, ImportGenius) selling customs records Market research publishers ("Germany Ceramic Tiles Market Size 2026-2032") Every one of those is a competitor, a middleman, or a report. None of them is a buyer. The first genuinely German distributor showed up below rank 10. So the hard part is not calling a search API. The hard part is precision: pulling a small number of real buyers out of a large volume of well optimised noise. The architecture below is built around that single problem. 2. Architecture product + country | v +----------------------+ 1 LLM call | 0. QUERY EXPANSION |<------------- translates the product and buyer vocabulary | extractor.py | into the target market's trade language +----------+-----------+ v +----------------------+ | 1. DISCOVER | DuckDuckGo (no API key) x N localised queries | search_agent.py | group hits by registrable domain | | drop directories, marketplaces, research, social | | deterministic pre-rank on cheap signals +----------+-----------+ v top ~20 domains +----------------------+ | 2. ENRICH | fetch home + contact + about + product pages | scraper.py | robots.txt honoured, thread pool, fails soft | | returns cleaned text + verified emails/phones/LinkedIn +----------+-----------+ v evidence bundle +----------------------+ 1 LLM call per candidate | 3. EVALUATE | Pydantic-validated structured output: | extractor.py | 5 independent criterion sub-scores + grounded reasoning +----------+-----------+ v +----------------------+ | 4. RANK | fixed weight vector, ceilings, dedupe, top-N | extractor.py | +----------+-----------+ v table + JSON + CSV (main.py) File Responsibility main.py CLI, stage orchestration, thread pools, progress, rendering, export search_agent.py Query building, keyless search with backend fallback, domain aggregation, noise filtering, pre-ranking scraper.py Bounded polite crawling, boilerplate stripping, contact extraction extractor.py Prompts, Pydantic schemas, LLM backends, scoring, ceilings, dedupe 3. Design decisions 3.1 The model scores criteria, Python computes the score The model never returns "this company is an 82". It returns five independent 0-100 judgements ( buyer_role_fit , product_match , market_fit , evidence_quality , contactability ), and the final number is a fixed weighted sum computed in compute_relevance_score() . Three reasons for splitting it this way: Consistency. Asking an LLM to "score this out of 100" produces drift between candidates and between runs. Asking "how strongly does the evidence show this company buys rather than manufactures?" is a narrower question and the answers are much more stable. Auditability. Every point in the final score traces back to a named criterion, and the full breakdown ships in the JSON output. A sales team can argue with the ranking on specific grounds instead of just distrusting it. Tunability. Re-weighting for a different exporter profile is a one-line dict change rather than a prompt rewrite. 3.2 Search stays deterministic, judgement goes to the model search_agent.py makes no LLM calls in its core path. Search results are noisy and free, so that stage optimises for recall using rules that are debuggable and reproducible. All the precision work happens during evaluation, where the model reads the company's own website. The one exception is the optional query expansion call described below, which is a translation task rather than a judgement task, and falls back to a built-in term table if it fails. 3.3 Query localisation An English query returns English-language SEO pages. A German query returns German companies. Before searching, one LLM call turns "Ceramic Tiles" plus "Germany" into local trade vocabulary such as Fliesen Importeur Großhandel or Keramikfliesen Distributor , and those queries run against a locale-matched search region ( de-de , derived automatically from --country ). In testing this produced German, Arabic and Dutch query sets from the same code path, including script changes. Disable it with --no-query-expansion and discovery falls back to a static local-term table covering about 25 markets. 3.4 Legal-entity name patterns This turned out to be the highest-precision discovery signal in the whole pipeline. Importers put their role in their registered company name, not in their meta tags. Manufacturers are the ones optimising for the word "importer". So alongside the obvious queries, the tool searches for local legal-entity patterns: Import Export GmbH , Handelsgesellschaft mbH , Vertriebs GmbH for Germany, General Trading LLC for the UAE, importadora Ltda for Brazil, and so on for about 20 markets. Adding those patterns took the Ceramic Tiles to Germany run from one genuine buyer in twenty candidates to three genuine buyers in the top three. 3.5 Cheap pre-ranking protects the expensive stages Scraping and LLM evaluation cost time and money. Search results do not. A deterministic signal score (query breadth, search position, buyer-vocabulary hits, product-token hits, domain geography) orders candidates so --max-candidates spends its budget on the strongest leads. The most useful single signal is the domain itself. A .de domain on a German market search scores +18, while .in , .cn and .pk domains score -25, because for an Indian exporter an Indian domain is almost always a competitor. It is a penalty rather than a ban, since an Indian-owned distributor registered in the target market would be an excellent lead. A trading word in the domain ( fliesen-import.de , xyz-handelsgesellschaft.de ) adds another +20. 3.6 Contacts are extracted by code, then selected by the model The model is never asked to produce an email address. It picks one from a verified list that scraper.py pulled off the actual pages, and _normalise_contact() discards anything the model returns that is not in that list. A hallucinated ceo@company.com cannot reach the output. Matching is tolerant of reformatting but not of invention. Models routinely rewrite 07071 / 151-151 as +49 7071 151-151 , which is the same line and should not be thrown away, so comparison falls back to matching trailing digits. Extraction itself is precision-first, because an exporter acts on these values: mailto: and tel: links are read first, since they are unambiguous a bare number in body t

page_title: Living Ceramics attends Orgatec; an essentially international fair targeting emotions and creativity - Livingceramics
text_content: Living Ceramics attends Orgatec; an essentially international fair targeting emotions and creativity - Livingceramics Living Ceramics attends Orgatec; an essentially international fair targeting emotions and creativity 18 September 2019 As part of its strategy to raise its profile beyond the ceramic tile sector, Living Ceramics made its debut at Orgatec, which took place in Cologne between 23 rd and 27 th October. Throughout 2018, Living Ceramics has channelled major efforts at its production facilities in Onda, Castellón, into developing technologies capable of producing smart large format ceramic tiles featuring relief surfaces. The company’s key objective is to offer the market unique cutting-edge ceramic tile solutions. The company was eager not to miss out on the excellent opportunity the Orgatec trade fair provided to present these innovations before the highly demanding German public Orgatec 2018 boasts a consolidated position at the forefront of the work culture sector, addressing key emotional issues and offering the entire sector new sources of creative inspiration. “Orgatec has successfully managed to transform itself from a mere product showcase to a business event focusing on highly relevant work culture-related issues”, explained Katharina C. Hamma, Operations Director at the Koelnmesse exhibition site, adding, “Thanks to a first class event and congress programme, Orgatec has effectively transmitted the socio-political importance of new contemporary work models to strategic decision makers”. The new trade fair concept received an enthusiastic reception: with more than 63,000 delegates, Orgatec 2018 amply exceeded last year’s figures with visitor numbers rising by 15%. The company was extremely pleased with the results of its debut as an exhibitor at the fair, and was impressed by the standard of visitors as well as the enthusiastic reaction to the products presented. meta_description: Find answers to all your questions in our BAU A-Z. Find important information regarding your exhibit at a glance.
text_content: Information for BAU exhibitors from A-Z Exhibitor FAQ You would like to become an exhibitor at BAU München and have questions about registration? Or are you already registered as an exhibitor and have questions about placement, trade fair planning or other exhibitor topics? Here you will find answers to frequently asked questions from our BAU exhibitors. FAQ topics General Application Placement Admission / Invoicing Trade fair planning General Where do I find the latest floor plan? Here you can find the floor plan of BAU Where can I find the BAU product index? The product index can be found under the exhibitor application under Exhibition sectors Application How do I apply as an exhibitor? Here you will find the online application as well as information on prices and conditions for main exhibitors. The registration deadline for main exhibitors is 10. January 2027. After a successful application, the main exhibitor will receive a link to the online application for co-exhibitors. The registration deadline for co-exhibitors is 10. January 2027. How do I register a co-exhibitor? When registering online, the main exhibitor receives a link that the co-exhibitor can use to register directly at this stand. By forwarding the link, the main exhibitor authorizes the co-exhibitor to exhibit at his stand. He hereby confirms that his co-exhibitor will be represented with staff and with his own offer, rights or services. If you wish to register as a co-exhibitor, please contact your main exhibitor directly. The registration fee per co-exhibitor is 1.000.00 EUR. A mandatory communication fee of 1.300.00 EUR will be charged for each co-exhibitor. The registration deadline for co-exhibitors is January 10, 2027. How do I register as a start-up? Here you can find the registration for the start-up area. Where can I find the prices for participating at BAU? All information on prices and conditions can be found on our price page . Is the registration binding? The application for BAU is non-binding until the placement proposal has been confirmed by you, i.e. cancellation of the application is possible until then without causing any costs. Nevertheless, we do require your completed online application in advance in order to be able to properly manage your data for the placement. What happens if I want to cancel my application? An application is first non-binding and not linked to any costs. Cancellation fees will only be charged if you wish to return your stand space after your confirmation of the placement proposal. Cancellation of stand space must always be sent in written form to bau.projektleitung@messe-muenchen.de. If Messe München GmbH is able to re-rent the stand space to a new exhibitor, the cancellation fees will amount to 25% of the participation fee plus the entry fee. If re-renting is not possible, 100% of the participation fee. The registration fee will not be charged. The exact rules of a contract cancellation can be found in the General Conditions of Participation A under A5. Where can I find my contacts? You will find your contact persons for BAU on our Advice & Contact page . You can also send an e-mail to b au .p ro je kt le it un g@ me ss e- mu en ch en .d e Placement When does the stand allocation start? The planning of the halls begins in autumn 2025. The placement proposals will then be sent out from spring 2026. The placement proposal will include your exact positioning in the specific hall. Can I provide a preferred placement? With your registration you can request your preferred stand positions. During the planning phase, we will do our best to take into account the stand requests of all registered companies. However, please understand that we cannot fulfill all wishes. Admission / Invoicing When will I receive the admission invoice? You will receive the admission invoice after your placement proposal is confirmed from May 2026. The payment deadline is October 1, 2026. The admission invoice includes the following items: Stand space Registration fee Mandatory communication fee Disposal fee AUMA fee The Association of the German Trade Fair Industry (AUMA) charges all exhibitors a fee of EUR 0,60 per square meter of rented exhibition space. This contribution is calculated by Messe München GmbH and paid directly to AUMA. Further information on advance payment for services: The advance payment for services to be ordered refers to all services that you can order for the trade fair via Exhibitor Services online in the Exhibitor Shop. This includes, for example, electricity, water, compressed air, vouchers for customer invitations, etc. The amount will be invoiced per square meter. The services you actually order will be balanced against this advance payment amount when the final invoice is generated - either you will then only pay the difference or you will receive a refund. Waste disposal fee: The obligatory waste disposal fee of EUR 10.00 per square meter covers the disposal of waste generated by the exhibitor on his stand during set-up and dismantling, as well as during the entire duration of the trade fair. The disposal of production waste, complete stand elements and complete exhibition stands is excluded from this. Mandatory communication fee: All exhibitors will be charged a mandatory communication fee of EUR 1.300.00 for each of their stands. The obligatory communication fee includes the basic entry in the trade fair media as well as further communication services (digital or printed, see B 12 Media Services). You are only authorized to participate in the trade fair after payment of your admission invoice. Is there an electronic invoice mailing service? In your application you can specify whether you would like to receive our invoices as a PDF document attached to an e-mail or whether you would like to receive the invoices as a print-out by mail. If you agree to receive invoices electronically, we ask you to provide a non-personalized e-mail address of your accounting department, if possible, which is accessible to all employees of your accounting department. Trade fair planning Where can I find the exhibitor shop? The BAU Exhibitor Shop will be available for placed exhibitors from summer 2026 at the following link: Exhibitor shop How do I book services for my trade fair presentation? If you require special services for your trade fair presentation, you can contact Messe München GmbH's Exhibitor Services. You can find all further information here: Services for exhibitors (messe-muenchen.de) In addition, you will find the exhibitor shop here. How can I contact the Technical Exhibitor Service (TAS)? Our Technical Exhibitor Service (TAS)—Department 3 will assist you with any questions and orders regarding the technical equipment for your stand. E-mail: t as 3@ me ss e- mu en ch en .d e Our TAS team is also there for you directly on site at the trade fair. The exhibitor service offices at the exhibition center are located in the atrium in front of the hall B2. Staffing and opening hours vary depending on the event. Where can I find the traffic guide? Our traffic guide will lead you quickly and safely to the trade fair center and inform you about the entry and deposit regulations. The traffic guide will be available for download on the page Logistics & Traffic in good time before BAU. Which logistics companies can I contact for transportation? Our two official logistics companies, Kühne + Nagel and Schenker Deutschland, offer you worldwide and national transport to the Munich trade fair venue, as well as customs clearance and on-site handling, including stand delivery and temporary storage. Furthermore, they support you with all other logistical challenges in connection with your trade fair appearance. How do I get my exhibitor passes as an exhibitor? Each exhibitor receives free exhibitor passes depending on the size of his stand. You can find the scale in our prices and conditions. You can access the ticket management via the Exhibitor Shop. text_content: March 2026 Tiles Exhibition: Guide to Global Tile & Ceramic Fairs - Ramirro March 2026 Tiles Exhibition: Guide to Global Tile & Ceramic Fairs Ramirro Ceramica Last Updated on - February 7, 2026 - Published on February 7, 2026 March 2026 Tiles Exhibition Guide: MosBuild, Coverings, Salone del Mobile, Expo Revestir, Ceramics Africa, ceramitec & Uniceramics Expo March 2026 marks one of the most important periods on the global tile calendar, bringing together some of the world’s most influential tile, ceramic, and surface exhibitions in a short window of time. From MosBuild and Coverings to Expo Revestir, Ceramics Africa, ceramitec, Uniceramics Expo, and the design driven influence of Salone del Mobile, this season shapes product direction, material performance standards, and design conversations for the year ahead. This guide breaks down each exhibition in the order they take place, explaining what truly matters for architects, designers, distributors, and project planners without hype or confusion. Written from the perspective of Ramirro Ceramica, a global tile manufacturer focused on design integrity, technical performance, and real world application, the article helps readers move beyond trends and make informed tile decisions that work on site, not just on display.
